name: J.Press
why: Ivy League clothing — the sack suit, the oxford shirt, the Shaggy Dog Shetland sweater — largely unchanged since the early 1900s.
origin: Founded on the Yale campus in 1902 by Jacobi Press; owned by Onward Kashiyama of Japan since 1986.

notes.ivy: the source code — the same sack suit since 1902, canonized by the 1965 Japanese photo book Take Ivy
notes.finbro: the uniform of the finance bro's grandfather — law professors, old Washington, the bow-tie corner of the firm
notes.prep: The shop the Preppy Handbook actually names, still on the same streets. Where other brands reference the register, this one is a primary source for it.
notes.racquet: New Haven, and the squash-club register is close to native — the shop was built to dress the people who were already members. Little translation required.

notes.craft: J.Press says many products are made in America (New York, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Georgia) and elsewhere, but names no factory it owns. Its product pages give a country on nearly every item and name the cloth mill for tailoring and dress shirts (Marling & Evans tweed, Thomas Mason). Named mills and clear countries, nothing owned: a 3.

cities: 3 stores — New Haven, New York, Washington, and its own site

marks: On house goods: NONE. Harris Tweed 7 (licensed protected cloth appellation, not a performance technology)
Shaggy Dog 15 (house garment name, never carries (R))
merino 21 / elastane 2 composition_only. All true technology marks on the site sit on STOCKED third-party labels

craft_evidence.owned_d: No owned factory named. History page: 'many of our products are made by hand in America — in New York, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Georgia, and more — as well as in Japan, Scotland, England, Italy, and Canada' — states, not factories. Site organises 'Made in USA/Scotland/Italy/Canada/Japan…' collections, i.e. multi-country partner sourcing. Parent Onward Kashiyama (per worklist origin_line) not checked for owned factories making J.Press US product.
craft_evidence.countries: Product feeds across 3 collections (10 sport coats, 11 shirts, 19 sweaters = 40): USA 15 (all sport coats, 5 dress shirts), Scotland 18/19 sweaters, India 6 madras shirts (3 by tag 'Made in India', 3 by 'woven in India' only); 1 sweater no country. Rendered sport coat PDP confirms 'Made in USA' in visible copy.
